descriptionChirho: A noun (tsori) denoting an aromatic resin or balm, prized for its medicinal and healing properties, produced in Gilead. Used as a trade commodity (Gen 37:25, 43:11; Ezek 27:17), and as a metaphor for spiritual healing (Jer 8:22 'Is there no balm in Gilead?', 46:11, 51:8). Multilingual evidence is uniform: eng 'balm', spa 'bálsamo', hin बलसान, arb بَلَسَانًا/بَلَسَانٌ, kor 유향, swa 'zeri/balm'. The article in S130733 is a syntactic feature (interrogative context), not a separate sense.
